claims.description: The persisted redemption schema stores only HMAC digests and bound non-secret authority fields, constrains issued completeness, and uniquely serializes one verifier handle and one provider evidence identity.

The verifier service commits an issued receipt before returning, reconstructs exact retries, validates receipts during attachment, rejects mutated or concurrent attempts, bounds provider calls with a timeout, emits structured failure outcomes, and releases only undecided reservations for retry.

Real PostgreSQL regressions cover ordinary success, response loss and exact retry, concurrent duplicate redemption across two connections, mutated tuples, provider success followed by lost persistence, token-without-receipt rejection, and transport failure followed by successful same-handle retry.
The mobile callback retains the minted authority token after initiation so attachment failure retries do not attempt to consume the provider handle again.
The complete migration sequence including the durable redemption table replayed against a disposable PostgreSQL database and the repository prepush gate passed.
